task: Repair release-unit successor obligation drift classification so the first canonical sealing of unchanged operations is treated as trusted reprojectable provenance enrichment while any semantic operation change or resealing/tamper remains material fail-closed drift.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: The bounded multi-release-unit rehearsal successfully merged U01 through trusted exact-head child proof, then U02 failed closed with RELEASE_UNIT_EXECUTION_OBLIGATION_DRIFT because fresh successor projection canonically sealed otherwise unchanged create operations with source commit/blob/fileMode provenance. The current classifier compares raw operation JSON and therefore cannot distinguish deterministic first-time sealing from a real operation mutation. This blocks resumable successor execution even though the immutable parent source and semantic operation set are unchanged.
observableOutcomes: A successor whose unsealed operations are enriched only by canonical sealing metadata from the immutable parent source is classified as reprojectable rather than material drift.
The associated childOperationDigest change is reprojectable only when both the before and after digests exactly match their own operation sets and the operation delta is canonical first sealing.
Any semantic operation change such as file, operation type, rename source, generated semantics or intended content remains material fail-closed drift.
Any already-sealed operation whose source commit, blob SHA or file mode changes remains material fail-closed drift.
Trusted fresh projection is still required before a reprojectable sealing enrichment can be accepted.
The live rehearsal can resume at U02 without modifying the immutable parent source or bypassing release-unit proof.
unresolvedRisks: Blindly stripping source metadata from comparison would permit sealed-source tampering.
Treating childOperationDigest as reprojectable without verifying both operation digests would weaken binding integrity.
Allowing resealing from one source identity to another could silently substitute content.
A helper that compares operations by position rather than stable operation identity could produce false acceptance when ordering changes.
The fix must not weaken existing tests that intentionally classify real operation path drift as material.

in: Refine release-unit obligation drift classification in scripts/lib/shoperation-release-unit-runtime.mjs.
Recognize only first canonical sealing provenance enrichment where semantic operation identity is unchanged and fresh sealing is internally coherent.
Classify childOperationDigest as reprojectable only when the corresponding operation change is canonical sealing and both digests match their own operation arrays.
Add regression coverage for accepted first sealing, untrusted projection rejection, semantic operation drift, resealing/tamper and digest mismatch.
out: No change to sealReleaseUnitManifest source/blob derivation.
No change to materializeReleaseUnit write behavior.
No global removal or ignoring of operation source metadata.
No relaxation of forbidden/read-only path checks, predecessor receipts, main lease, Truth, Lifecycle or child CI proof.
No change to storefront, template, Supabase or deployment code.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This classifier decides whether persisted release obligations may be safely reprojected after predecessor merge. A permissive mistake could permit source substitution or operation tampering; an over-strict mistake deadlocks valid resumable execution. The fix therefore needs provenance-specific invariants and negative tamper cases.

acceptanceCriteria: Unsealed operations plus canonical source metadata only are identified as provenance enrichment, not semantic operation mutation.
Canonical enrichment requires after.sourceIdentity.sealed=true and a non-empty immutable sourceCommit.
Every fresh operation must preserve all non-source fields exactly.
Fresh sealed/regenerate/delete source metadata must match the canonical source contract for its operation kind.
Before and after child operation digests must each equal strongDigest of their own operation arrays before digest drift can be considered reprojectable.
Trusted fresh projection remains mandatory to accept the reprojectable drift.
Already-sealed source identity changes remain material drift.
Existing genuine operation-drift regression remains fail closed.
Exact-head CI, Completion Truth and Lifecycle Closure pass before merge.
invariants: Semantic operation scope is never widened by provenance reconciliation.
Source provenance is never ignored globally.
Only the first transition from unsealed to canonical sealed provenance may be reprojectable.
A sealed source commit/blob/fileMode may not mutate through this path.
Operation digests remain cryptographically bound to the exact operations they summarize.
Trusted fresh projection provenance is required for acceptance.

failureModes: Classifier still marks canonical first sealing as material drift.
Classifier accepts a real operation mutation because source metadata also changed.
Classifier accepts resealing to a different immutable source.
Classifier accepts an operationDigest not derived from the corresponding operations.
Classifier accepts reprojectable drift without trusted fresh projection.
Ordering-only differences create false semantic mutation.
edgeCases: before operation has no source; after has sealed source with same non-source fields
regenerate operation gains mode=regenerate source metadata
before and after are both sealed and identical
before sealed commit A; after sealed commit B
same operations but incorrect after operationDigest
operation file path changes during sealing

alternatives.summary: Detect a narrowly defined first canonical sealing transition, verify provenance and operation digests, and classify only that delta as reprojectable under trusted fresh projection.
alternatives.reason: Preserves immutable source security while allowing the intended successor re-evaluation lifecycle.

alternatives.summary: Strip source metadata before all operation comparisons.
alternatives.reason: Would hide source commit/blob/fileMode tampering and weaken the sealed-source contract.

alternatives.summary: Add operations and childOperationDigest to the global reprojectable field set.
alternatives.reason: Would permit real material operation changes under trusted projection and defeat the hard obligation boundary.

alternatives.summary: Manually rewrite the persisted rehearsal U02 obligation to match the fresh manifest.
alternatives.reason: Would bypass the general defect instead of repairing resumable execution semantics.

specialistReviews.finding: Treating all operation source metadata as non-semantic would erase an important source-integrity boundary.
specialistReviews.resolution: Permit only first canonical sealing with exact non-source equality and immutable source contract checks; already-sealed changes remain material.

specialistReviews.finding: Blob/commit provenance is security-sensitive and must remain fail closed after sealing.
specialistReviews.resolution: Require before unsealed, after sealed, one canonical sourceCommit, valid per-operation source shape and digest self-consistency.

specialistReviews.finding: childOperationDigest changed only because canonical provenance was added, but digest acceptance must not become independent of operation identity.
specialistReviews.resolution: Reproject the digest only as a dependent consequence of a verified canonical sealing transition and self-consistent before/after digests.

specialistReviews.finding: U01 exact trusted child proof #9077 succeeded and PR #1053 merged; the next blocker is isolated to U02 successor reconciliation.
specialistReviews.resolution: Repair classifier generically, merge it on exact proof, then replay the same immutable parent source and require U02 to advance without manual state mutation.

specialistReviews.finding: The live rehearsal exposed a previously untested interaction between source sealing and successor obligation drift classification.
specialistReviews.resolution: Add positive and adversarial regression cases before replaying the rehearsal.

challenge.scenario: Unsealed create operation gains canonical sealed commit/blob/fileMode and nothing else changes.
challenge.finding: Current raw JSON comparison reports material drift.
challenge.resolution: Classify as sealing enrichment only after full provenance validation.

challenge.scenario: Same first sealing occurs but trustedFreshProjection=false.
challenge.finding: Fresh provenance has not been authorized by trusted projection.
challenge.resolution: Keep it STALE until trusted fresh projection is true.

challenge.scenario: File path changes while source metadata is added.
challenge.finding: This is semantic operation drift disguised as sealing.
challenge.resolution: Non-source operation equality must fail and keep material drift.
First-sealing predicate requires before.sourceIdentity.sealed!==true; resealing remains material.

challenge.scenario: Already-sealed operation keeps commit but changes blobSha/fileMode.
challenge.finding: Would permit content or mode substitution.
challenge.resolution: Already-sealed provenance changes remain raw material operation drift.

challenge.scenario: Operations look like valid first sealing but after operationDigest is forged.
challenge.resolution: Require both before and after childOperationDigest to equal strongDigest of their own operation arrays.

challenge.scenario: Delete/regenerate operations have different canonical source shapes.
challenge.finding: One generic sealed-source shape would reject valid cases or accept invalid ones.
challenge.resolution: Validate delete source:null, regenerate source.mode=regenerate, ordinary operations source.mode=sealed.

challenge.scenario: Operation array order changes but semantic operations are identical.
challenge.finding: Order-only drift should not become a hidden material mutation or bypass.
challenge.resolution: Use the same stable sorted-object comparison already authoritative for obligations while validating one-to-one semantic operation identity.

challenge.scenario: Fresh projection changes authorities/evidence plus canonical sealing in the same successor pass.
challenge.finding: Live U02 contains both reprojectable policy drift and provenance enrichment.
challenge.resolution: Both categories may be reprojectable under trustedFreshProjection; any independent material field still blocks.

requirements.requirement: Successor reconciliation must distinguish canonical first-time sealed provenance enrichment from real material operation drift without weakening immutable source integrity.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: An already-sealed operation may not change source commit/blob/fileMode through successor reprojection.
A semantic operation change may not be reclassified as canonical sealing enrichment.
Canonical sealing enrichment may not be accepted without trusted fresh projection provenance.

notes: Live bounded multi-release-unit rehearsal evidence: U01 trusted workflow_dispatch CI #9077 passed and PR #1053 merged at main 12447f0cfd73abe8728209ea3f35cb132a9b06d4. Release Unit Execution #184 then failed at U02 with RELEASE_UNIT_EXECUTION_OBLIGATION_DRIFT because initial unsealed operations were canonically enriched with sealed source metadata, changing both raw operations JSON and childOperationDigest. This plan repairs the generic classifier; it does not mutate persisted rehearsal state or weaken operation/source integrity.
